thread.drunk_smith.drinking: Hammer's heavy of a morning. Heavier every morning, it seems.
One cup to wash the soot down. Then another for the ache. You know how it goes.
Don't look at me like that. The iron doesn't care if my hands shake.
thread.drunk_smith.complaints: So the reeve's hinges cracked. Bad iron, I told him. Bad iron.
They talk behind my back at the well. I hear them. I'm not deaf, only thirsty.
The lad does half the work now. More than half, if I'm honest. I'm not, mostly.
thread.drunk_smith.debt: The steward wants his coin by the rest day. I've got slag and a sore head.
I owe the tavern, I owe the charcoal man, I owe the steward. Everyone but the devil, and he's patient.
If someone paid it off I'd swear off the drink. I would. Ask the priest, he's heard me swear before.
thread.drunk_smith.vowing: The priest wants candles for the vow. Good wax, mind, not tallow.
Bring the candles and I'll kneel. Before I lose my nerve.
thread.drunk_smith.vowed: I swore before the altar. The candles burned all night. I've been dry four days.
My hands still shake, but they shake over the anvil now, not the cup.
thread.drunk_smith.sworn_off: Water. Water and bread. My head's never been so clear, nor my temper so short.
The tavern keeper looks at me like I've died. Maybe I have, a bit.
thread.drunk_smith.sober: Sober a month. The lad's back at the bellows and the hinges hold.
I owe you. Come by the forge; I'll make you a blade at cost, and a good one.
Funny thing. The iron sings when you can hear it.
thread.drunk_smith.forge_lost: The forge is the lad's now. He's good. Better than I was, these last years.
I sit by the gate and watch the carts. Somebody has to.
Don't pity me. Buy me a cup, if you must do something.
thread.widow_at_well.mourning: I come to the well because we came together. Silly, isn't it.
The bucket's lighter than it was. Everything is, without him to carry for.
Good of you to stop. Most walk faster when they see me.
thread.widow_at_well.alone: The house is so quiet I hear the mice arguing.
The roof leaks over his side of the bed. I can't bring myself to see to it.
Sit a moment, would you? Just a moment.
thread.widow_at_well.comforted: I laughed yesterday. At a goat. First time since the funeral.
You were kind to me when nobody had the time. I won't forget it.
thread.widow_at_well.new_purpose: Six of the little ones today. They wear me out and I sleep like a stone.
A house wants noise in it. Now mine has plenty.
thread.widow_at_well.withdrawn: I'm going to my sister's. There's nothing here but the grave.
thread.young_lovers.secret: If you see {partner} at the stile tonight, you didn't see anything. Understand?
Our fathers haven't spoken in years. Over a ditch. A ditch!
thread.young_lovers.found_out: They found us. My father said things I won't repeat, and {partner}'s mother threw a pot.
They'd sooner see us both in the river than wed. Will nobody speak for us?
We could go. Tonight. If we had a little coin for the road.
thread.young_lovers.blessed: They said yes. Both of them! I think my father was relieved, the old goat.
The banns go up soon. You'll come to the wedding? You must.
thread.young_lovers.forbidden: I'm watched day and night. I see {partner} across the square and we can't even nod.
It'll pass, they say. As if they know.
thread.young_lovers.eloped: We're going. Don't try to stop us.
thread.young_lovers.parted: It's over. {partner} won't look at me now.
Let the houses keep their feud. I've nothing left for it to take.
thread.ambitious_apprentice.eager: I'm up before the cock. Someone has to light the fire, and I like to have it hot.
My master says I rush. I say the work doesn't wait.
thread.ambitious_apprentice.asks: If I had the iron I could make my masterpiece now. Why wait two more seasons?
Bring me what I need and I'll show the guild. I'll show them all.
My master would say no. So I'm not asking my master.
thread.ambitious_apprentice.waiting: Six good ingots, that's all. Then you'll see.
thread.ambitious_apprentice.early_master: The guild drank to me. Me! Before my time, they said, and they meant it kindly.
I won't forget who helped me to it.
thread.ambitious_apprentice.humbled: So you told on me. Fine. Maybe I needed telling.
The master says patience is half the trade. I'm learning the other half first.
thread.ambitious_apprentice.patient: My time comes when it comes. The work's better for the waiting.
thread.ambitious_apprentice.resentful: Held back, that's what I am. Held back by an old fool who fears the competition.
There are towns where a journeyman gets a fair chance.
thread.ambitious_apprentice.left: I'm off. There's a guild in the next town that'll know my worth.
thread.old_soldier.war_story: Did I tell you about the ford? Three days we held it. Three days, in the rain.
The young ones don't listen. They think war is banners and songs.
Sit. You've the look of someone who's never been told about the ford.
thread.old_soldier.banner: I lost my blade at the ford. Dropped it in the mud when the bolt took me. Forty years and I still reach for it.
A soldier without his sword is just an old man on a bench.
You'd not have time for the whole of the story, I suppose.
thread.old_soldier.heard: You listened to all of it. Nobody has, since my wife.
I'll teach the lads the drill, I think. Before it's lost with me.
thread.old_soldier.seeking: A plain blade, mind. Nothing with gilt on it. We weren't gentry.
thread.old_soldier.blade_home: It hangs over my door, see? I take it down of a morning and the boys come running.
You've given an old man back his name. I won't forget it.
thread.old_soldier.drills: Left foot! Your other left! Gods, the ford would have eaten you alive.
They'll stand in a line now. That's more than the lord's men can do.
thread.old_soldier.fading: Cold today. The old wound knows it before the sky does.
I'll tell you about the ford another day. Not today.
thread.gossip.whispers: Have you heard about {partner}'s lot? No? Come closer.
I don't say it's true. I only say what I heard. That's different.
thread.gossip.spreading: Everybody knows about {partner}'s house now. Not from me, of course.
If it isn't true, why does {partner} go so red when it's mentioned?
You look like someone who knows things. Tell me something.
thread.gossip.quashed: Well. Perhaps I had it wrong. It happens to the best of us.
You took the fun out of the whole week, you know that?
thread.gossip.feud_brews: I never meant for it to come to fists. Words are just words.
{partner}'s lot won't speak to mine now. Is that my fault?
thread.gossip.shunned: Nobody tells me anything any more. I'm the last to hear of a birth.
thread.gossip.forgotten: Old news, that. Now, about the miller's wife...
thread.miser_merchant.hoarding: A bit saved is a bit earned. Twice earned, if you count the interest.
Charity? I give the gift of fair prices. Well. Prices.
thread.miser_merchant.refuses: The town wants my coin for a well. Let them drink from the river like their grandfathers.
Everyone has a hand out. I keep mine in my pockets.
You won't shame me into it. Better folk have tried.
thread.miser_merchant.gives: Fine. Fine! Put my name on the well, at least. In big letters.
They tip their hats to me in the street. Strange. Not unpleasant.
thread.miser_merchant.robbed: Robbed! Robbed in my own house! Where was the watch? Where was anyone?
Every bit I had. Every last bit.
thread.miser_merchant.humbled: When it was all gone, the neighbours brought me bread. The neighbours. I never gave them so much as a nail.
I give a little now. It's cheaper than being alone.
thread.miser_merchant.alone: Nobody calls. Good. Callers want things.
thread.healer.short: Yarrow, comfrey, willow bark. I've a pinch of each and a town full of coughs.
If a fever comes now I'll be treating it with prayers and hot water.
You've the look of someone who walks the woods. Bring me what grows there?
thread.healer.gathering: Ferns from the shade and berries from the edge of the wood. That will do to start.
thread.healer.stocked: The shelves are full. I can sleep again.
Whatever comes, we'll meet it now.
thread.healer.fever: The fever's in three houses. I go from bed to bed and there's nothing in my bag.
Coin would buy what the pedlar has. Coin I haven't got.
thread.healer.saved: Every one of them on their feet. Every one.
They bless your name in the houses that had the fever. I made sure they knew it.
thread.healer.lost_one: I couldn't save the little one. I keep going over it, every leaf, every hour.
thread.runaway.restless: Where does the road go, past the bridge? Have you been? What's there?
Everyone here dies where they were born. Not me.
thread.runaway.plans: I've a bundle under the bed. Bread, a knife, a blanket. That's all you need, isn't it?
A few bits for the road and I'd be off tonight.
thread.runaway.watched: You told. I can't step out to the privy without someone following.
thread.runaway.stays: The road will keep. There's work here, and it's not so bad.
thread.poacher.snares: The lord's deer eat our barley. Seems fair the barley eats a deer now and then.
I'm out walking of a night. For my health. Very good for the health, the woods.
thread.poacher.suspected: They found snares by the oaks. Could be anybody's. Could be yours, for all they know.
If anyone asks, I was home. You'd say so, wouldn't you?
A haunch of venison for a short memory. Fair trade.
thread.poacher.covered: You're a friend. I don't forget friends.
Quieter now. The steward's watching the oaks.
thread.poacher.caught: A day in the pillory and a rotten cabbage in the ear. Could have been the rope.
Somebody talked. I know somebody talked.
thread.poacher.reformed: The lord made me his huntsman. Who knows the wood better?
I catch the poachers now. I know all their tricks. They were mine.
thread.miller_in_debt.debt: The stones need dressing, the wheel needs a new paddle, and the debt needs paying. Pick one.
I borrowed from {partner} in the wet year. The wet year's long gone; the debt isn't.
thread.miller_in_debt.pressed: {partner} wants it all by harvest, or the mill.
My father's mill. His father's. And I'll lose it for a bad year.
Would you speak to {partner}? They might listen to someone who isn't me.
thread.miller_in_debt.eased: A season's grace. A season! I could kiss you. I won't. But I could.
thread.miller_in_debt.free: Every bit paid. The wheel sounds different now. Lighter.
Bring your grain to me any time. I'll not take the miller's toll from you.
thread.miller_in_debt.mill_lost: {partner} has the mill. I grind for wages now, at my own stones.
Don't say {partner}'s name in my hearing.
thread.pious_pilgrim.vow: I have vowed to walk to the shrine, as my mother did. Barefoot, if my feet allow it.
Alms for the road, friend? A bit for every league, and I'll pray for you at each.
thread.pious_pilgrim.blessed_road: With your alms I'll eat on the road. I'll light a candle for you at the shrine.
thread.pious_pilgrim.returns: I went, and I came back, and the candle burned for you. Here, from the shrine.
My feet are ruined and my heart is light.
thread.exile_come_home.returned: Twelve years gone and they look at me like I left yesterday, with the silver.
I wasn't a good man when I left. I'm a better one now. Nobody believes it.
thread.exile_come_home.old_wrong: {partner}'s house remembers. Every word I said, every door I broke.
If someone would vouch for me to the elders. Someone they'd listen to.
Or I could earn my place. If I had tools to start with.
thread.exile_come_home.welcomed: They set a place for me. My mother cried into the soup.
{partner} shook my hand. Stiffly. But they shook it.
thread.exile_come_home.settles: Work's the best answer to talk. They'll come round, or they won't.
thread.exile_come_home.leaves: There's nothing for me here. There never was.
